references.text: Jesus gives similar instructions to the twelve disciples not to take gold, silver, copper, a bag, two tunics, sandals, or a staff – parallel to the instructions given to the seventy in Luke 10:4.
When Jesus sent out the twelve, he gave corresponding instructions not to take a staff, bag, bread, money, or extra clothes – a close parallel within the Gospel of Luke itself.
Mark's version of the sending of the twelve includes similar exhortations not to take bread, a bag, or money, and to wear sandals – related to the travel instructions in Luke 10:4.
Jesus refers back to the sending and asks the disciples if they lacked anything when he sent them out without a purse, bag, or shoes – a direct reference to Luke 10:4.
Elisha sends Gehasi and tells him not to greet anyone he meets along the way – parallel to Jesus' command not to greet anyone on the road.
The context of the verse: Jesus sends out the seventy (or seventy-two) two by two ahead of him into every town and place where he himself was about to go.
Paul urges believers not to worry about anything – a similar trust in God's provision that underlies Jesus' instructions not to carry a purse or bag.
Jesus' words about not worrying about food, drink, or clothing express the same principle of trust in God's care that lies behind the instructions in Luke 10:4.
